hypothesis: THP on top of the PGO champion (THP has never been tested on Graviton5, and the earlier c8g "win" was host drift). 4.9% of light-phase samples were page faults, almost all in jemalloc arena growth, and each heavy call builds ~1 MB of storage maps; THP=always backs that anonymous memory with 2 MiB pages. Tests whether a system lever still stacks on top of a PGO build.
llm_commentary: Re-baseline on the rebuilt harness, which times the request phases rather than the whole script. Stock 5.02s workload (light 1.71s, heavy 3.34s) → champion 3.19s (light 1.39s, heavy 1.78s): -36.5%, against the -33.3% the old wall-clock metric reported for the same two builds. The gap is the dilution now measured directly: a steady 1.42-1.48s of node startup, genesis init and teardown sat inside every previous number, so all historical deltas understate the workload gain by roughly a seventh. Phase attribution now comes from a single run instead of separate profiled ones, and it is sharper than expected: heavy -46.6% (the three storage commits plus PGO) versus light -18.3% (the rayon handoff plus PGO). Two caveats for comparison: (1) old and new figures are NOT interchangeable — anything compared against pre-harness numbers must be re-measured, (2) the stock run trips the new noise flag at 3.4% spread while the champion sits at 2.1%; the metric is more sensitive now that a constant 1.4s no longer damps the variance, so the 3% threshold is worth revisiting rather than treating 3.4% as a defect.
